content.title: Interstate 80
content.text: INTERSTATE 80 Number of Miles- 2909 California- 195 miles Nevada- 410 miles Utah- 197 miles Wyoming- 401 miles Nebraska- 455 miles Iowa- 301 miles Illinois- 163 miles Indiana- 167 miles Ohio- 236 miles Pennsylvania- 314 miles New Jersey- 68 miles Eastern End- Teaneck, NJ at I-95 Western End- San Fransisco, CA at US 101 Major Cities Along the Route- San Francisco , CA Oakland, CA Sacramento, CA Reno, NV Salt Lake City, UT Cheyenne, WY Omaha, NE Des Moines, IA Chicago, IL Gary, IN Cleveland, OH New York City Area Intersections with other Interstates I-5 in Sacramento, CA I-15 in Salt Lake City, UT I-84 in Echo, UT I-25 in Cheyenne, WY I-76 near Big Spring, NE I-35 in Des Moines, IA I-29 in Council Bluffs, IA I-74 in Bettendorf, IA The Western I-88 near Moline, IL I-74 near Moline, IL I-39 in La Salle, IL I-55 in Joliet, IL I-57 in Tinley Park, IL I-94 in South Holland, IL. They stay joined until Portage, IN. I-90 in Portage, IN. They stay joined until Clearview, OH I-65 in Gary, IN I-69 near Fremont, IN I-75 in Toledo, OH I-71 in Strongville, OH I-77 in Brecksville, OH I-76 in Niles, OH I-79 in Pardoe, PA I-81 in St Johns, PA I-95 in Teaneck, NJ Spur Routes- The Bay Area (SF/Oakland, CA)- I-280, I-380, I-580, I-680, I-780, I-880, I-980 Cheyenne,WY- I-180 Lincoln, NE- I-180 Omaha, NE- I-480, I-680 Spur to Waterloo, IA- I-380 The Quad Cities- I-280 Spur to Hennepin, IL- I-180 Toledo, OH- I-280 Cleveland, OH- I-480 Youngstown, OH- I-680 Spur to Williamsport, PA- I-180 Spur to Scranton, PA- I-380 Spur to The Oranges, NJ- I-280 Notes First let me say that if I-80 were the first highway I had to do, I would never have started this project. This road has more intersections in the middle of nowhere (thank you IL) and whacky connections with other roads (including being joined with I-90 for most of IN and OH) than any 5 other Interstates. It also has I-180 in Cheyenne, which is an interstate with traffic lights (thanks to Mark Bozanich for pointing this out to me). I have no idea what is up with that. It can be argued that I-80 goes all of the way to the George Washington Bridge, but I think that's just silly. :) Return to the Interstate List
